tldr: This thread is a label, not one event: four unrelated arXiv papers that share the words "anomaly detection". The October pair targeted video and few-shot industrial inspection, and the August papers it replaced covered relational data, ICS security and streaming video.
whats_new: Two Nov 9 papers push anomaly detection toward cheaper inference: LogCDM flags log anomalies from behavioral-graph drift without GPU-bound language models, and Vendi Anomaly Scores proposes a diversity-based score in place of density or isolation heuristics.
why_it_matters: The shared direction is cost: three of the four papers explicitly target cheaper or lighter detection than dense VLM, exemplar-store or 8B-parameter log models, which is the constraint that decides whether a detector can run inside a monitoring or agent pipeline.

beats.headline: October papers trim the inference cost of vision anomaly detection
beats.summary: MoG-VLM uses motion cues to avoid dense frame-level VLM inference; Flownomaly models normality from a handful of defect-free images without tying inference to stored exemplars.

beats.headline: November papers target log monitoring and a new general-purpose anomaly score
beats.summary: LogCDM argues large pretrained log models are hard to deploy on monitoring hosts and offers an interpretable graph-drift alternative; Vendi Anomaly Scores redefines anomalies by diversity rather than density, isolation or distance.

open_questions: Does LogCDM match the detection accuracy of BERT-scale or 8B-parameter log models on standard log benchmarks while running CPU-only?
Does Vendi Anomaly Scores hold up on high-dimensional embedding data such as LLM traces, or only on the benchmarks the paper reports?
Does MoG-VLM report end-to-end latency on real-time video, or only reduced frame counts?
Do any of these papers release code an operator could run against production telemetry?
take_for_builders: Read LogCDM if your log anomaly detection needs GPU-hosted models today; skip the rest unless you run video or visual inspection, and wait for released code before planning a swap.

day_captions.10f91cbb4979cd0e: Uses motion guidance to cut the dense frame-level inference that makes VLM video anomaly detection impractical in real time.
day_captions.ad09687688336a6f: Few-shot industrial defect detection that avoids stored exemplars and rigid linear structure via single-step conditional-mean recovery.
day_captions.d1b93ef36fd4bf1f: Moves log anomaly detection off GPU-bound pretrained models to interpretable behavioral-graph drift with adaptive signal fusion.
day_captions.79a0f00b03e27450: Proposes a diversity-based (Vendi) anomaly score as an alternative to density, isolation and distance-from-distribution definitions.
